program.target: Frank v0.1 fully operational on accepted Hostinger Ubuntu VPS

question: Can the accepted target's Ubuntu SQLite 3.45.1 WAL path be behaviourally classified for the upstream WAL-reset corruption race, and can the deterministic fault harness distinguish the old line from fixed upstream SQLite 3.53.4?

internal_evidence.finding: V3 private SQLite 3.53.4 admission/composition passed on target with Python isolated mode, PYTHONPATH sqlite3 shadow rejection, V17 composition and UnifiedDB+ClayGraph pair smoke; whole Frank v0.1 acceptance not claimed.

Axis-D source/runtime identity binding passed, but the discriminator did not execute because reconstructed Ubuntu source configure rejected unsupported option --debug. This is a harness build failure, not a vulnerable/fixed SQLite result.

fresh_external_evidence.finding: SQLite documents the WAL-reset bug as likely present from 3.7.0 through 3.51.2 and fixed in 3.51.3 and later; trigger topology requires WAL, at least two connections, and concurrent write/checkpoint timing.
SQLite 3.53.4 is a fixed-line release and its release page carries the WAL-reset fix in the 3.53 lineage.

hypothesis: The exact accepted-target Ubuntu 3.45.1 source lineage remains behaviourally vulnerable to the WAL-reset fault and should stay excluded from correctness-sensitive Frank WAL state; the already target-green private 3.53.4 V3 path is the safer release candidate.
strongest_counterhypothesis: The Ubuntu package may contain an equivalent backport not obvious from version number, or the deterministic injected fault harness may itself produce corruption independently of the upstream WAL-reset bug and therefore be non-discriminating.

go_oob_experiment.name: METAMORPHIC_SAME_FAULT_OLD_VS_FIXED_SQLITE
go_oob_experiment.design: Inject the same deterministic sqlite3FaultSim(660) checkpoint fault into exact Ubuntu 3.45.1 source and upstream 3.53.4, then run the same integrity harness on the same target lane.
go_oob_experiment.falsifier: If both lines corrupt, both pass, or either result is unclassified, reject the harness as non-discriminating and do not promote the system-SQLite vulnerability claim from this experiment.

architecture_delta.change: Keep correctness-sensitive Frank WAL state fail-closed against system SQLite 3.45.1 while behavioural classification is unresolved; retain private pinned SQLite 3.53.4 under V3 isolated-Python admission as the currently stronger candidate. Product boot must still establish the -I boundary before any import-capable Frank Python.
architecture_delta.rollback: No system SQLite replacement, no canonical database mutation, no external effect. Drop PR #339 and retain previous fail-closed gate if the discriminator does not validate.
